def: Information about the target that reaches the model in training or validation but will not legitimately be available when the model is used.
Leakage from a feature that is recorded after the outcome, caused by it, or is the label under another name.
Leakage from a learned step such as scaling, imputation or feature selection being fitted on validation rows before the split.
Leakage caused by the same or near-identical examples appearing in both the training and the evaluation data.
Leakage from using information dated after the prediction time, for example a rolling window that extends into the future.
A column such as a row number, file name or site code that records how data was gathered and happens to correlate with the label.
A table listing each feature's source, the time it is written, whether it can change later and whether it is available at prediction time.
A join that attaches to each prediction only the most recent record that was already known at the prediction time.
A difference between how a feature is computed in training and how it is computed in production.
Training a classifier to tell training rows from test rows; an AUC well above 0.5 shows the sets differ and which columns give them away.
Scoring each feature alone by how well it ranks the target, to find columns that are suspiciously predictive.
